exercise_group.instructions: In Exercises 1–21, mark each statement True or False (T/F). Justify each answer.

statement.paragraph: (T/F) Given $\textbf{v}_{1}\text{,}$ $\textbf{v}_{2},\ldots,\textbf{v}_{p}$ in $\text{ℝ}^{n}$ and scalars $c_{1},\ldots,c_{p}$, an affine combination of $\textbf{v}_{1}$, $\textbf{v}_{2},\ldots,\textbf{v}_{p}$ is a linear combination $c_{1}\textbf{v}_{1} + \cdots + c_{p}\textbf{v}_{p}$ such that the weights satisfy $c_{1} + \cdots + c_{p} = 1$.﻿
(T/F) The affine hull of two points $\textbf{v}_{1}$ and $\textbf{v}_{2}$ is the set of all points $\textbf{y} = t\textbf{v}_{1} + (1 - t)\textbf{v}_{2}$, with $t$ in $\text{ℝ}$.﻿
(T/F) A hyperplane is a $\text{4-dimensional}$ flat.
(T/F) Two flats are parallel if their intersection is empty.
(T/F) Every subspace is a flat.
(T/F) Every subspace is an affine set.
(T/F) Every affinely dependent set is linearly dependent.
(T/F) Every affinely independent set is linearly independent.
(T/F) The barycentric coordinates of a point in $\text{ℝ}^{2}$ are always nonnegative.

(T/F) Let $S = \{\textbf{v}_{1},\ldots,\textbf{v}_{k}\}$ be an affinely independent set in $\text{ℝ}^{n}$. Then each point $\textbf{p}$ in $\text{ℝ}^{n}$ has a unique representation as an affine combination of $\textbf{v}_{1},\ldots,\textbf{v}_{k}$.﻿

(T/F) A convex combination of points $\{\textbf{v}_{1},\textbf{v}_{2},\ldots,\textbf{v}_{k}\}$ in $\text{ℝ}^{n}$ is a linear combination of the form $c_{1}\textbf{v}_{1} + c_{2}\textbf{v}_{2} + \cdots + c_{k}\textbf{v}_{k}$ such that $c_{1} + c_{2} + \cdots + c_{k} = 1$ and $c_{i} \geq 0$ for all $i$.﻿

(T/F) If a set $S$ is affinely independent and if $\textbf{p} \in \text{aff~}S$, then $\textbf{p} \in \text{conv~}S$ if and only if the barycentric coordinates of $\textbf{p}$ with respect to $S$ are nonnegative.
(T/F) The line segment between $\textbf{x}$ and $\textbf{y}$ is the set of all points of the form $(1 - t)\textbf{x} + t\textbf{y}$, where $t$ is in $\text{ℝ}$.﻿
(T/F) Every affine set is a convex set.
(T/F) For some $\text{ℝ}^{n}$, the dimension of a hyperplane can be the same as the dimension of a line.
(T/F) For some $\text{ℝ}^{n}$, the dimension of a hyperplane can be less than the dimension of a line.
(T/F) Suppose $A$ and $B$ are nonempty compact convex sets. Then there exists a hyperplane that strictly separates $A$ and $B$ if and only if $A \cap B = \varnothing$.﻿
(T/F) A polytope can be the convex hull of infinitely many points.
(T/F) Every nonempty compact convex set $S$ has an extreme point, and the set of all extreme points is the smallest subset of $S$ whose convex hull is equal to $S$.﻿

(T/F) If $\textbf{w}(t)$ is a quadratic Bézier curve with control points $\textbf{p}_{0}$, $\textbf{p}_{1}$, and $\textbf{p}_{2}$, then $\mathbf{w}\prime(0)$ has the same direction as the tangent to the curve at $\textbf{p}_{0}$ and $\mathbf{w}\prime(1)$ has the same direction as the tangent to the curve at $\textbf{p}_{1}$.﻿
(T/F) When two Bézier curves are connected with $G^{1}$ geometric continuity, then the tangent vectors for the two curves at the common control point have the same direction.
If $S = \{\textbf{v}_{1},\ldots,\textbf{v}_{k}\}$ is an affinely independent subset of $\text{ℝ}^{n}$, prove that $k \leq n + 1$.﻿
Suppose that $F$ and $G$ are $k\text{-dimensional}$ flats $(0 \leq k \leq n - 1)$ in $\text{ℝ}^{n}$ with $F \subseteq G$. Prove that $F = G$.﻿

Prove or give a counterexample: A set $S$ is convex if and only if for each $\textbf{p}$, $\textbf{q}$ in $S$, the set of points of the form $(1 - t)\textbf{p} + t\textbf{q}$, where $0 < t < 1$, is contained in $S$.﻿

Let $V$ be a $k\text{-dimensional}$ subspace $(0 \leq k \leq n - 1)$ of $\text{ℝ}^{n}$ and let $F_{1} = \textbf{x}_{1} + V$ and $F_{2} = \textbf{x}_{2} + V$ for vectors $\textbf{x}_{1}$, $\textbf{x}_{2}$ in $\text{ℝ}^{n}$. Prove that either $F_{1} = F_{2}$ or $F_{1} \cap F_{2} = \varnothing$. Thus two parallel flats either coincide or are disjoint.

Let $f$ be a nonzero linear functional on $\text{ℝ}^{n}$ and suppose $H = \lbrack f:7\rbrack$. If $\textbf{p} \in \text{ℝ}^{n}$, $f\left( \textbf{p} \right) = 2$, and $H_{1} = H + 3\textbf{p}$, then find $d$ such that $H_{1} = \lbrack f:d\rbrack$.﻿

Let $V$ be an $(n - 1)\text{-dimensional}$ subspace of $\text{ℝ}^{n}$ and suppose $\textbf{p} \in \text{ℝ}^{n}$ but $\textbf{p} \notin V$. Prove that each vector $\textbf{x}$ in $\text{ℝ}^{n}$ has a unique representation as $\textbf{x} = \textbf{v} + c\textbf{p}$, where $\textbf{v} \in V$ and $c \in \text{ℝ}$.﻿

If $m$ is the maximum value of the linear functional $f$ on the convex set $S$, and $\textbf{p}$, $\textbf{q}$ are points in $S$ such that $f\left( \textbf{p} \right) = f\left( \textbf{q} \right) = m$, show that $f(\textbf{x}) = m$ for all $\textbf{x}$ in $\overset{‾}{\textbf{pq}}$.﻿

If $B(\textbf{p},\text{δ})$ is the open ball with center $\textbf{p}$ and radius $\text{δ}$ in $\text{ℝ}^{n}$, prove that $\text{λ}B\left( \textbf{p},\text{δ} \right) = B\left( \text{λ}\textbf{p},\text{λ}\text{δ} \right)$, where $\text{δ} > 0$ and $\text{λ} > 0$. This means that dilations and nonzero contractions map circles in $\text{ℝ}^{2}$ onto circles and balls in $\text{ℝ}^{n}$ onto balls.

list.item: Show that the set {v1,v2,v3,v4} is affinely independent.
Let A=aff{v1,v2,v3,v4} and B=[f:3], where f is the linear functional defined by f(x1,x2,x3,x4)=x1+x2+x3−x4. Prove that A=B. Hint: Use Exercise 23.

exercise_group.instructions: Exercises 31–35 deal with the following concepts: A point $\textbf{p}$ is called a positive combination﻿ of the point $\textbf{v}_{1},\ldots,\textbf{v}_{k}$ if $\textbf{p} = c_{1}\textbf{v}_{1} + \cdots + c_{k}\textbf{v}_{k}$﻿, with all $c_{i} \geq 0$﻿. The set of all positive combinations of points of a set $S$ is called the positive hull of $S$ and is denoted by $\text{pos~}S$.

statement.paragraph: Let $S = \{( - 1,1),(1,1)\}$ in $\text{ℝ}^{2}$. Describe the set $\text{pos~}S$ geometrically.

Observe that in Exercise 31 we have $\text{pos~}S \cap aff~S = conv~S$. Show that this is not true in general by verifying the following example: Let $T = \left\{ \textbf{v}_{1},\textbf{v}_{2},\textbf{v}_{3} \right\}$, where $\textbf{v}_{1} = (0,1)$, $\textbf{v}_{2} = (1,1)$, and $\textbf{v}_{3} = (1,0)$. And let $\textbf{p} = (3,2)$. Show that $\textbf{p} \in \text{pos}~T \cap \text{aff}~T$, but $\textbf{p} \notin \text{conv~}T$.﻿
What special property does set $S$ in Exercise 31 have that makes $\text{pos~}S \cap \text{aff~}S = \text{conv~}S$?
Let $S$ be a nonempty subset of $\text{ℝ}^{n}$. Show that $\text{pos~}S = pos\,\text{(conv~}S\text{)}$.﻿
Let $S$ be a nonempty convex subset of $\text{ℝ}^{n}$. Prove $\textbf{x} \in \text{pos~}S$ if and only if $\textbf{x} = \text{λ}\textbf{s}$ for some $\lambda \geq 0$ and some $\textbf{x}$ in $S$.﻿
